source: Paths: OpenStreetMap (Overpass export, snapshot 2026-11-01T22:33Z) via the M4 draft graph, rebuilt with tools/osm_to_graph.py. Places: Daya's My Maps pins, plus OpenStreetMap building centres where marked. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

schema.node: id (see id_rules), name, group (core | faculty | college | transport | sports | health | landmark | junction), lat, lon, verified (true only once the pin is confirmed), position_source (places: where the pin came from), osm_node (junctions only: the point they sit on)
schema.junction_nodes: Nodes with group 'junction' are routing-only (path forks, start/end of a covered walkway or shaded stretch). They are hidden from the start/destination pickers.
schema.edge: id (see id_rules), from, to, distance_m, covered (bool), shade_score (0-1), flood_prone (bool), traffic_peak (bool), step_free (bool: false = has stairs or is not wheelchair-friendly), shade_by_hour (optional: {"7": 0-1, ..., "19": 0-1}), source (where the path came from, e.g. OpenStreetMap way ids), geometry ([[lat, lon], ...] along the real path); unknown values = null
schema.edge_direction: Edges are two-way. Store each path segment once; the app adds both directions when it loads the graph.
schema.distance_m: Computed from geometry (or the straight line between the two nodes if there is no geometry), not measured by hand.
schema.null_handling: TO CONFIRM WITH TEAM. Proposed: treat unknown values as worst case (covered=false, shade_score=0, flood_prone=true, traffic_peak=true) so unverified segments are never favoured. Alternative: reject edges with nulls when loading.
schema.how_edges_are_made: v0.4 was imported from the M4 draft graph (same OpenStreetMap export). Next rebuild: export with tools/um_paths.overpassql and run tools/osm_to_graph.py; tools/check_graph.py checks the result.
schema.step_free: For users with limited mobility (Firestore users.health.mobilityLimited). Stairs come from OpenStreetMap (highway=steps), so false is reliable; null means not tagged. Proposed: mobility-limited routes avoid edges with step_free=false (team to confirm).

known_issues: 12 places use the centre of their OpenStreetMap building outline and are verified=false: UMC, ENG, LAW, FAB, APIUM, PASUM, CLINIC, KK4, KK5, KK11, LRT, MASJID. Move each pin to its main entrance, then set verified=true and re-run tools/osm_to_graph.py.
KK5: 64 m from the nearest mapped path; a path may be missing in OpenStreetMap.
APIUM -> KK8 is 3.6 km by path against ~960 m in a straight line: OpenStreetMap may be missing a shortcut, or it is private.
covered: only known where OpenStreetMap tags it (103 of 452 edges); check the rest on satellite/Street View.
shade_score: ROUGH ESTIMATE from the draft (0.9 covered, 0.5 within 12 m of a building, 0.2 otherwise; no trees). Replace with the tree-canopy and building-shadow calculation.
flood_prone: unknown everywhere; fill from news articles, the survey and hazard reports.
step_free: false on the 19 stair segments from OpenStreetMap; everything else unknown.

id_rules.place: Short ALL CAPS abbreviation people would recognise, 2-8 letters/digits, e.g. FSKTM, LIB, KK8. No '-'.
id_rules.junction: J + 3 digits, e.g. J012. Given once, never changed, never reused (id_counters remembers the last one).
id_rules.path: START-END with the two node IDs in alphabetical order, e.g. FSKTM-J012. A second path between the same two points gets -2, a third -3 (e.g. J012-J013-2). Matches the nearestEdgeId example in docs/firestore-schema.docx.
id_rules.stability: Re-running tools/osm_to_graph.py keeps every existing junction ID; only new junctions get new numbers.
id_rules.code: Code must never read meaning out of an ID (use the from/to fields instead of splitting the ID at '-').
